patterns.fix: Bundle every script inside the package. Replace eval and remote fetch with local code and local data files.
signals: script tag with an http or https src outside the package
eval() on a string fetched from a remote source
new Function() on a remotely fetched string
an interpreter that runs commands fetched as data

patterns.fix: Vendor the module into the package and import it by relative path.
signals: import of a module from a remote URL
dynamic import of a remote URL

patterns.fix: Ship readable source. Remove obfuscation, minification that hides intent, and encoded code blobs. Minified builds are allowed only when the source stays readable on inspection.
signals: eval() or the Function constructor used on a string
dense hex or unicode escapes (\xNN, \uNNNN) in code
long base64 blobs that decode to code

patterns.fix: Migrate to Manifest V3. MV2 extensions are no longer accepted for new submissions.
signals: manifest_version is 2
manifest_version missing

patterns.fix: Open the submitted ZIP, not the dev folder, and check every path the manifest names exists with the exact same case.
signals: a file named in manifest.json is missing from the package
an icon, background script, popup, options page or content script path that does not exist
case mismatch between the manifest path and the real filename

patterns.fix: Either build the promised feature or cut it from the listing. If the extension needs an account or a special network setup, say so in the listing and leave test credentials in the reviewer notes.
signals: a feature the listing promises that the code never implements
the extension does nothing on first run without an account, and the listing never says so

patterns.fix: Remove the permission. If the API is genuinely used, keep it and write the justification in the dashboard: what it does, and which visible feature needs it.
signals: a permission declared in the manifest with no matching API call in the code
tabs declared but only tabs.query used for the current tab
activeTab declared alongside broad host permissions that already cover the same access
cookies declared but only document.cookie used
storage declared but only localStorage used

patterns.fix: Narrow host access to the domains the extension actually works on. Broad host access almost always forces manual review, which takes days to weeks, and it reads as a red flag to the reviewer.
signals: host_permissions set to <all_urls>
host_permissions set to https://*/* or http://*/*
content_scripts matches set to <all_urls>

patterns.fix: Remove it now and add it back in the release that actually needs it. Pay the slow review once, for a real reason.
signals: a permission used only by a debug or dev-only feature
a permission kept just in case for a future feature

patterns.fix: Fill every field. The title names the job, the description lists the major features in plain sentences, and every screenshot shows the extension in action.
signals: blank description field
missing icon, title or screenshots
a title that is not meaningful or is misleading
screenshots that do not show the extension doing its job

patterns.fix: Make the listing and the code describe the same product. State every behavior in the metadata. You may offer the same functionality as another extension, but do not copy from it.
patterns.notification: Red Nickel, Red Potassium, Red Silicon
signals: the listing promises functionality the extension does not provide
the extension does something the listing never mentions
the extension pretends to be authorized or produced by another company
the extension copies another extension's code, name or branding

patterns.fix: Remove the claim and the testimonials. Only verifiable facts belong in the listing.
patterns.notification: Red Nickel, Red Potassium, Red Silicon
signals: metadata that claims an award, rank or status the extension does not hold, such as Editor's Choice or Number One
unattributed or anonymous user testimonials in the description

patterns.fix: Put a working privacy policy URL in the designated Privacy Policy field, and make the policy describe every type of data collected, how it is used, and how it is shared.
signals: the code collects user data but no privacy policy exists
the privacy policy pasted into the description instead of the designated field
the privacy policy URL is dead, unreachable, or does not lead to a privacy policy
the policy never mentions collection, use, handling or sharing

patterns.fix: Disclose the collection prominently in the listing and inside the extension before collection starts, get consent, and collect only what the stated purpose needs.
signals: data collected without telling the user first and getting consent
data collected that is not in direct support of the single purpose

patterns.fix: Send user data only over HTTPS, in the request body, never in URLs or headers.
signals: user data sent over plain HTTP
user data encoded in request headers or query parameters, even over HTTPS

patterns.fix: Stop collecting browsing activity unless a visible feature requires it, and never publish collected user data.
signals: Web Browsing Activity collected when no user facing feature needs it
collected user data disclosed publicly

patterns.fix: Split the extension. One purpose per extension, stated in one sentence. Secondary features are acceptable only when they serve the primary purpose and could not stand alone as their own product.
patterns.notification: Red Magnesium, Red Copper, Red Lithium, Red Argon
signals: two or more unrelated purposes in one extension
an unrelated extra feature behind the action icon
a New Tab Page or search provider override bundled with other features
ad injection bundled with any other functionality

patterns.fix: Rewrite the description as plain sentences about what the extension does. Use each keyword in context, once or twice, and delete the lists.
signals: the same keyword repeated unnaturally more than 5 times in the description
a long list of sites, brands or locations in the metadata
lists of keywords without substantial added value

patterns.fix: Ship one extension per purpose. Do not touch reviews or install numbers, keep notifications quiet, and never send anything as the user without their consent.
signals: multiple extensions from the same developer with duplicate functionality
manipulated reviews, ratings or install counts
disruptive notifications
messages sent on behalf of the user without consent

patterns.fix: An extension that only opens a website is not allowed. Build the functionality into the extension itself.
signals: the only functionality is opening another app, theme, webpage or extension
a promotional page for another product shown immediately after install

patterns.fix: Ship a real feature that runs inside the extension and delivers the value the listing promises.
signals: a package containing nothing but a manifest
no discernible value or utility
a claimed feature that only links out to an external service
clickbait metadata designed to attract installs

patterns.fix: Disclose the affiliate use in the description and in the UI, and only include affiliate codes after a related action by the user.
signals: affiliate links, codes or cookies used without disclosing them in the description and UI
affiliate codes included without a related user action first

patterns.fix: Market the extension plainly. The button says install, the page says what it installs, and nothing hides the listing.
signals: unclear or hidden disclosures on marketing pages before the listing
call to action buttons that imply an outcome other than installing the extension
resizing the listing window to hide metadata

patterns.fix: Use the Overrides API for New Tab Page and search changes, or do not make them.
signals: the New Tab Page changed without the Overrides API
the omnibox search changed without the Overrides API

patterns.fix: Remove the feature. If the paywall or download bypass is the primary functionality, the extension cannot be listed at all.
patterns.notification: Blue Zinc, Blue Copper, Blue Lithium, Blue Magnesium
signals: access to content behind a paywall or login
facilitating download of YouTube videos
facilitating download of content the user has no right to

patterns.fix: Stop. Continued attempts end in suspension of the developer account.
signals: manipulating the store state or listing to evade review
holding users on older versions to dodge enforcement

patterns.fix: Remove the content, or mark the extension Mature where that is the only issue. If the banned content is the primary purpose, unpublish.
patterns.notification: Grey Zinc, Grey Copper, Grey Lithium, Grey Magnesium, Grey Nickel, Grey Potassium, Grey Silicon
signals: illegal activity
online gambling or prediction markets
pornographic content
hate content
violent content
cryptocurrency mining
content not suitable for all ages without the Mature flag

patterns.fix: Keep the listing under the character cap and review every field on each release.
signals: description longer than 16,000 characters
category, developer name or promo images out of date or inaccurate

patterns.fix: Narrow matches to the exact domains and paths the features need.
signals: host permissions granted to domains the extension never contacts
content_scripts matches wider than the sites the extension works on

patterns.fix: Ship against the production backend and leave working test credentials in the reviewer notes field.
signals: the extension needs a backend that is down, in staging, or unreachable at review time
no test account left in the reviewer notes for a login-gated feature
